RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel alone is not evidence of discrimination; women frequently make up leadership and hiring panels in education. While you possess stronger formal administrative qualifications, principal appointments heavily weigh interview performance, strategic vision, references, and institutional fit. 

Raising the panel’s gender without concrete evidence of bias is legally groundless and could severely damage your professional reputation and future career prospects in the district. 

Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting your written feedback. Once received, examine whether objective scoring rubrics or procedural standards were violated. Focus strictly on qualifications, merit, and hiring procedures rather than the demographic composition of the committee.
